subject: MSA / Order Form: security exhibit exception request and evidence cadence
messages:
From: Chris Nolan <chris.nolan@praxishealth.com>
To: olga_petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>, laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Maggie Chen <maggie@procurement.praxishealth.com>

Subject: Security exhibit — request to narrow inspection scope and align evidence cadence

Hi Olga / Laura,

Thanks again for the walkthrough last week. Our legal and infosec teams ran a quick review of Redwood's MSA + security exhibit and we're trying to avoid a full "inspection" clause that requires live access to production environments. In short: Praxis is OK with SOC 2 attestation and a rolling pen-test report, but we need the order form to explicitly limit inspection to sampled, scheduled windows (we propose 2x per year) and to carve out ephemeral credential requests to a staging environment only.

Two asks from our side:
- Can Redwood accept a bounded inspection clause (timebox + scope) instead of unlimited audit rights?
- Can you propose a practical evidence cadence (what items we'll receive, and when) so procurement can map to our compliance calendar?

I've attached a marked-up PDF of the redlines from our counsel. If it helps, we can introduce our external counsel (Tom Alvarez at ClarkLegal) into the thread.

Appreciate a quick outline of options — we need language to move procurement forward this week.

Thanks,
Chris

--
Chris Nolan
Director, IT Risk & Compliance
Praxis Health

Subject: Re: Security exhibit — request to narrow inspection scope and align evidence cadence

Chris — thanks for sending this and for the clear asks. I looped in Laura (legal) and Karthik (commercial counsel) to propose defensible language and a recommended evidence cadence. Quick notes from product/security: Redwood wants to avoid opaque carveouts that meaningfully reduce our ability to verify our controls, but we're open to a bounded approach (scheduled windows + sampling) for enterprise customers in regulated sectors.

Proposed next steps from our side:
1) Laura to propose redline language that limits inspection to scheduled, documented windows and to require a written request 30 days in advance.
2) Karthik to surface any commercial implications (SLA/carveouts) and confirm whether we can accept a 2x/year sampling cadence.
3) Ben to outline what evidence we can bundle (SOC 2 report, pen-test summary, system architecture diagram, sanitized logs, role-based access control matrix) and the expected delivery timeline.

Can you confirm whether Praxis needs raw logs or only aggregated/sanitized artifacts? That will drive whether we keep inspection to staging only.

I'll follow up by EOD with an initial redline.

—Olga

Subject: Re: Security exhibit — request to narrow inspection scope and align evidence cadence

Chris — appreciate the mark-up. I reviewed Praxis's proposed edits and drafted alternate language that should balance their need for assurance with Redwood's operational constraints. Key points in the redline:

• Inspection window: Limit to two (2) scheduled inspection windows per 12-month period. Requests must be submitted at least 30 days in advance.
• Scope: Inspections limited to systems and logs directly supporting the Redwood inference runtime provisioned for Praxis; no full-cloud tenant-wide access.
• Staging carveout: Ephemeral privileged access to production systems is not permitted; any active testing should occur in staging or a mirrored environment where feasible.
• Evidence package: On request, Redwood will provide SOC 2 report, executive pen-test summary (redacted by default), architecture diagram, role-based access lists, and a one-time sample of sanitized logs for the inspected components.
• Escalation / Counsel: If Praxis requires additional forensic evidence or raw logs, Redwood will consider a mutually agreed SOW with payment for on-premise or enhanced forensic access.

I'll attach the PDF redline and include the precise clause language if that helps your procurement counsel. If Praxis accepts these limits, we can reflect them in the order form (section: Security Exhibit — Inspection Rights).

Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Contracts & Compliance
Redwood Inference
Attachments: Redwood_limitied_inspection_redline.pdf (proposed clause)
From: ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: olga_petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>, Chris Nolan <chris.nolan@praxishealth.com>, laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 27 Oct 2026 09:46:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Security exhibit — request to narrow inspection scope and align evidence cadence

Thanks — adding a brief technical note to the legal framing so procurement can see what we can deliver without operational risk:  

- SOC 2 report: 30 days after request (we can provide most recent full report).
- Pen test: We provide an executive summary and risk rating within 10 business days of request; full raw pen-test artifacts (vulnerabilities + payloads) are retained by our security team and only released under a narrow NDA/SOW for forensic work.
- Logs: We can provide sanitized, sampled logs (redacted PII, trimmed to relevant services) within 10 business days; for live systems we prefer to provide this as an export, not live access.
- Staging access: We can offer a staging mirror with representative traffic for deeper testing — this requires 2-week lead time and basic configuration support from Praxis (we'll share a runbook).
- Evidence cadence suggestion (we also attached a one-page cadence spreadsheet):
   * Annual SOC 2 (full report) — baseline — shared by Redwood within 30 days of request
   * Pen-test executive summary — upon request + annual scheduled summary
   * Rolling sampled logs & RBAC snapshot — per inspection window (2x/year)

If Praxis wants unlimited inspection rights, operationally we will need to convert that to an SOW that covers the time and effort to support live collection and forensic review. Happy to jump on a 30-minute call to work through specifics.

Ben Carter
Principal, Security Solutions
Redwood Inference
From: Chris Nolan <chris.nolan@praxishealth.com>
To: olga_petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>, laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Security exhibit — request to narrow inspection scope and align evidence cadence

Team — this is very helpful, thanks. Tom (copied) from ClarkLegal confirms the proposed language should be workable for our counsel if Redwood adds a short sentence that calls out the SOW route for any forensic-level requests and clarifies that SOC 2 + exec pen-test summary are the baseline deliverables.

Praxis accepts the 2x/year scheduled windows, 30-day notice, staging-only ephemeral access, and the evidence package Laura outlined. We have one final ask: can Redwood confirm turnaround SLAs for each deliverable (Laura/Ben note already helpful — can you put those SLAs into the order form appendix so procurement can sign off)?

If you can send a redlined MSA + a short appendix listing the deliverables and SLA days, we can get procurement + legal to sign off and fast-track the PO. Chris — I can review the attached redline and will confirm this afternoon.

Next steps agreed:
- Redwood to send redlined MSA (with the inspection clause and a 1-page evidence SLA appendix).
- Praxis counsel to confirm and return a final signature-ready order form/PO.

Thanks again — I think this is close.

Chris
